current.text: He is a projected starter for the Knicks, next to Brunson, Hart, Anunoby and Towns.
He faded after a hot start last season. Late in the season he was benched in closing lineups, played under 30 minutes, took about one free throw per game and had a usage rate of about 16 percent.
Experts say he was outside standard category league value for the last two to three months of last season, around 130th per game.
Gavin expects the same small late-season role this season. Mike Brown may cut his role further if he struggles.
Experts call him one of the most overpriced players. Do not draft him at his ESPN rank of 26 to 29 or at a market ADP in the 50s to 70s.
His fair value is around pick 98, in the 90s.
In auctions Josh values him at about 2 USD and does not like him in head-to-head leagues. He went for 10 USD in an auction mock.
The Knicks play a league-minimum 13 back-to-backs. Their fantasy playoff schedule is weak for a season ending March 28.

Experts disagree on Knicks rest. Earlier notes expect trimmed starter minutes and more rest over the first 30 or so games after the title run. The newest note says a weaker team in a stronger East may not be able to rest players as much.
The Knicks are projected to win about 50 to 54 games.

durable.text: He is very durable and has never missed a game.
He can be projected to play more games than the usual player, but Josh warns he will get hurt at some point.
He avoids contact and does not attack the rim, so he gets few free throws.
He is an elite off-ball defender.
He is a low-volume, solid-percentage player with some steals and threes, few turnovers and no clear standout category.
Nine-cat totals flatter him, because his games played add value that his per game line does not.

note: ESPN prices him at 26 USD (rank 29), but every expert note says to fade him and puts his fair value near pick 98, or about 2 USD in an auction. That is close to his Yahoo average cost of 2.2 USD and below the 9 USD our league paid last season. His per game line has no weak category, so he fits any build as a cheap late filler with steals, threes, low turnovers and full availability. Do not pay more than a few USD. Early in the season, check whether he plays over 30 minutes and closes games. The Knicks also have a weak playoff schedule for our March 28 end.
